clue.text: O. a letter used to spell 'brook'

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are put to use spelling something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note that a single letter O spells out a river's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to spell' tells you to rearrange O, A and LETTER; 'brook' is the verb, to put up with, not a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to endure or allow it, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Excellent execution

explanation.surface: A first-rate hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping is old British slang for first-rate; to top someone is slang for to kill, often by hanging.

clue.text: He could be mentorial — to cats

definitions.text: He could be mentorial — to cats

indicators.note: the letters of the next word might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who acts as a tutor to big felines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges MENTORIAL; the whole clue also describes the circus trainer of big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer who trains lions acts as a guide and master to the big cats.

clue.text: Setting out the indefinite article

indicators.note: the letters are not fixed in shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar point explaining 'a' and 'an'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indefinite' rearranges ARTICLE; the grammar term 'indefinite article' is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is an account or narration, a setting forth of facts.

clue.text: I advance, following army in the rear

indicators.note: the first piece comes after the army in the answer's order

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
to advance money is to lend it

explanation.surface: A soldier moves forward behind the troops at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail end is the last part, at the back of something.

clue.text: Man wearing an alien strip

indicators.note: the man is dressed in the other piece, so it wraps around him

parts.note: une is the French, so foreign, word for 'an'
Rob is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man is clothed in some extraterrestrial costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alien' means foreign, so 'an alien' is a foreign word for 'an'; 'wearing' sets the man inside it, as a body inside clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take one's clothes off, taking off a robe.

clue.text: Where to put cedilla or accent

explanation.surface: Instructions on placing marks on letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla sits beneath a letter, under the line; to accent a point is to emphasise it, stress it.

clue.text: Search revealing smuggled liquor

parts.note: to run contraband is to smuggle it
sack is an old name for dry white wine such as sherry

explanation.surface: Customs officers find contraband drink in a search.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search a place thoroughly and roughly.

clue.text: Continue to ask, and one gets a flower

parts.note: to beg on is to keep pleading
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A persistent asker is rewarded with a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The begonia is a popular flowering plant.

clue.text: Talked at length' about plagiarism being denounced

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: to prose is to talk tediously at length, so prosed
a crib is something copied from another's work

explanation.surface: Someone lectured long on literary theft and was condemned for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container; the apostrophe after 'length' is a printing stray. 'Plagiarism' is copying, schoolboy slang for which is a crib.
explanation.definitionFit: Proscribed means condemned or outlawed, so publicly denounced.

clue.text: Nearly but not quite dark

indicators.note: the word is given short of its full length, losing its final letter

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: It is almost, though not entirely, dark outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for almost or close to.

clue.text: Contractors enter this too

explanation.surface: Builders get involved in this as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties to a contract go into a deal together; the idiom also means additionally, as well.

clue.text: State doctor went ahead and took a risk

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A state doctor pressed on regardless and took a chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambled means bet or ventured something on an uncertain outcome.

clue.text: Runner very bad about money in competition

parts.note: the emu is a flightless bird that runs

indicators.note: the bad word goes around the money, enclosing it

parts.note: lousy means very bad
L stands for pound, libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: An athlete performs poorly over prize money in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside LOUSY; 'Runner' is a flightless bird, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulously means in a spirit of rivalry, trying to equal or outdo others.

clue.text: Shall I clean kitchen pans as youth starts to provide sustenance for invalids?

indicators.note: the beginnings of each of these words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A young helper asks whether to scrub the pans before feeding the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the first letters of Shall I Clean Kitchen Pans As Youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid to an employee off work through illness keeps them going.

clue.text: Aristocratic girl's name

parts.note: Patricia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl with a posh-sounding name.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrician means noble, belonging to the upper class, as Rome's patricians did.

clue.text: It's hard, what can be held responsible for damage

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an armful is as much as the arms can hold

explanation.surface: Something tough, it seems, is to blame for the breakage.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmful means causing injury or hurt.

clue.text: Going round with a doctor, one with a medical speciality

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
I is the Roman numeral one
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A doctor on rounds with a specialist colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' is the definition, encircling, not a ward round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient means surrounding or encompassing, as with ambient air.

clue.text: Salt, one absorbed by weaver

indicators.note: the single letter is taken into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: Silas Marner is the weaver in George Eliot's novel
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Salt being soaked up by a textile worker.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned sailor.

clue.text: Delegates about to frame pressman

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: to set up someone is to frame them
ED, short for editor, is a newspaperman

explanation.surface: Representatives are on the point of incriminating a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses SETUP plus ED, giving the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to assign it to someone else, a verb sense.

clue.text: Put up round high ball — a help in the game

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole string is raised, so read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: O is round in shape
a lob is a ball hit high
aid is a help

explanation.surface: Throwing a ball high in a game aids play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' signals reversal: in a down clue the pieces are read upwards. Diabolo is a juggling game: a spool spun and tossed on a string between two sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling toy and pastime played with sticks and string.

clue.text: Bill mountain-climbing with Jack, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue the word rises, so it is read upwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
the jack is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A man named Bill goes mountaineering with his friend Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses ALP. 'Bill' looks like a man's name beside Jack; it is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice posted up in public, a poster.

clue.text: In other words, go without finally finishing back-cloths, etc.

parts.note: sc., scilicet, is Latin for namely, that is to say

indicators.note: the letter is taken away from the other piece

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

indicators.note: the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: To put it another way, leave without completing the stage backdrops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes G (the last of 'finishing', picked by 'finally') from ENERGY, leaving ENERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Painted backdrops and flats on a stage make up the theatre set.

clue.text: Houri for whom Strelitzia was named?

definitions.text: Houri for whom Strelitzia was named?

parts.words: Houri for whom Strelitzia was named?
parts.note: a houri is a beautiful maiden of the Islamic heaven, and the strelitzia plant has a common name taken from a bright tropical bird

explanation.surface: A celestial maiden lends her name to a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Strelitzia, a South African plant, takes its popular name from the brilliantly plumed New Guinea bird; 'bird' is also slang for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is literally a girl from heaven, and the plant is named after the bird.

clue.text: Some animals, not all, are bad-tempered

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only a few creatures, not every one, are grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mean can mean being nasty or ill-natured, as in a mean dog.

clue.text: Boast I shone a lot in play

indicators.note: the letters are set in motion and rearranged, as in a game

explanation.surface: An actor brags about how brightly he starred in the drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges I SHONE A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to brag or exaggerate.

clue.text: Like The Tempest', a tale about Milan's leader

indicators.note: the story is placed around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: the first letter, the one at the head of the word

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's play is a story involving the Duke of Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M, the first of Milan's, inside STORY; Prospero in The Tempest is the deposed Duke of Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: The play is named after a tempest, a violent gale at sea, so it is storm-like.

clue.text: We only do dances without animation

indicators.note: the letters move around as if dancing, so are rearranged

explanation.surface: Our dancing is stiff and lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodenly means stiffly, without expression or liveliness.
